newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Crown Cork in Colombian canning joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Crown Cork in Colombian canning joint venture.

text.p: Colombia's Ardila Lulle industrial conglomerate Monday announced a joint venture with U.S. packaging company Crown Cork & Seal Co. Inc. to set up a $40 million canned drinks plant.
The new company, Crown Colombiana SA, will build the factory, which is expected to begin operations by the end of 1997, in Tocancipa, about 60 miles north of Bogota.
"We will be canning beer, sodas, malted beverages and other soft drinks," said Carlos Alberto Beltran, chairman of soda manufacturer Gaseosas Postobon -- flagship of the Ardila Lulle group.
"We hope this will enable us to expand our market share in the canned drinks market. We are also thinking about exporting."

Beltran said the plant will include a two-piece can manufacturing line and have an initial production capacity of 600 million cans per year. Output could be doubled as market conditions dictated, he added.

Ardila Lulle is one of Colombia's major drinks manufacturers, producing 572 million gallons of beer and soft drinks per year. Its major rival is the Santo Domingo industrial conglomerate, which includes brewing giant Bavaria SA.
The Ardila Lulle group imports most of its cans from Panama, Puerto Rico and Mexico. Cork Crown's stock rose $1.25 to $53.125 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
